subject: Mathematics
headline: Mathematicians are wanted across finance, software and engineering — three of the fastest-growing parts of the UK economy to 2030.

subject: Further Mathematics
headline: Further Mathematics opens the deepest routes into engineering, computing and defence — sectors the UK has picked to drive growth.

subject: Statistics
headline: Statisticians and data analysts are named priority occupations across digital technology, life sciences and finance.

subject: Computer Science
headline: Programmers are the single most in-demand role in the UK economy, needed in seven of the ten sectors the government is prioritising to 2030.

subject: Biology
headline: Biologists feed Life Sciences, one of the fastest-growing UK sectors, plus an NHS workforce being deliberately expanded.

subject: Chemistry
headline: Chemists are needed across clean energy, life sciences and advanced manufacturing — three of the UK's eight growth-driving sectors.

subject: Physics
headline: Physicists are wanted across clean energy, defence and digital technologies as the UK builds new power, security and computing capacity.

subject: Applied Science
headline: Applied scientists keep laboratories running across manufacturing and life sciences — lab and pharmaceutical technicians are in shortage.

subject: Environmental Science
headline: Environmental scientists are needed as the UK expands offshore wind, nuclear and other clean energy — one of its fastest-growing sectors.

subject: Psychology
headline: Psychology opens routes into an NHS workforce being deliberately expanded, from clinical psychology to a much bigger talking-therapies workforce.

subject: Engineering
headline: Engineers are needed across advanced manufacturing, clean energy and defence, where 6.3 million people already work in engineering and tech.

subject: Design & Technology (Product Design)
headline: Product design sits between advanced manufacturing and the creative industries — both sectors the UK has picked for growth.

subject: Health & Social Care
headline: Health and care roles are the single largest source of new jobs the government has identified — 90,000 more care workers needed by 2030.

subject: Construction & the Built Environment
headline: Construction is booking one of the fastest growth rates of any sector, driven by 1.5 million new homes and clean energy infrastructure.

subject: Business Studies
headline: Business graduates are wanted across professional and business services — England's single largest priority sector by employment.

subject: Economics
headline: Economists and analysts feed financial and professional services, where finance and investment roles are among the fastest-growing.

subject: Accounting
headline: Accountants remain in high demand nationally even as AI reshapes finance roles, according to the profession's own body, ICAEW.

subject: Law
headline: Solicitors are a growing priority occupation, and fast-expanding apprenticeship routes are opening up access to the legal profession.

subject: Geography
headline: Geography feeds planning, environment and construction roles as the UK builds homes and clean energy infrastructure at record pace.

subject: History
headline: History graduates take some of the most broadly transferable skills into any career, from heritage and archives to law and public service.

subject: Politics
headline: Politics graduates reach the government's priority occupations at a notably high rate — higher than law, media or psychology graduates.

subject: Sociology
headline: Sociology graduates feed the social care and public sector workforce, which the government is expanding as demand for care rises.

subject: Philosophy
headline: Philosophy's rigorous reasoning is valued across law, policy and the professional services that recruit graduates from any discipline.

subject: Religious Studies
headline: Religious Studies builds the same transferable reasoning and communication skills that open routes into education, law and public service.

subject: Criminology
headline: Criminology opens routes into policing, probation and the courts, where the justice system offers a steady, well-established career path.

subject: English Language
headline: English Language graduates take strong communication skills into publishing, media, teaching and the wider creative economy.

subject: English Literature
headline: English Literature remains a proven route into publishing, media, education and the wider creative industries.

subject: English Language & Literature
headline: Combining language and literature builds the communication skills that employers across media, education and business value most.

subject: French
headline: Language graduates reach the government's priority occupations at a notably high national rate — French opens routes into trade and teaching.

subject: Spanish
headline: Spanish is one of the world's most spoken languages, and language graduates reach the government's priority occupations at a high rate.

subject: German
headline: German underpins UK trade with Europe's largest economy, and language graduates reach priority occupations at a notably high rate.

subject: Chinese (Mandarin)
headline: Mandarin is a strategic language for UK trade and diplomacy, and language graduates reach priority occupations at a notably high rate.

subject: Art & Design (Fine Art)
headline: Fine art feeds the Creative Industries, a growth-driving sector where several art occupations sit on the UK's own shortage list.

subject: Graphic Communication
headline: Graphic and multimedia designers are named on the UK's shortage list and are one of the Creative Industries' fastest-growing roles.

subject: Photography
headline: Photography and broadcasting roles are projected to need 11,000 more workers by 2030 as the Creative Industries keeps expanding.

subject: Textile Design
headline: Textile design sits inside a UK fashion and textile industry worth £62 billion, spanning design, making and sustainable fashion.

subject: Film Studies
headline: Film and TV is a named frontier industry inside the Creative Industries, a sector the government has picked to drive national growth.

subject: Media Studies
headline: Media graduates reach the government's priority occupations at a strong rate, from journalism and PR to marketing in the creative economy.

subject: Music
headline: UK music supports a record 220,000 jobs and contributed £8 billion to the economy in 2024 — and orchestral musicians sit on the shortage list.

subject: Music Technology
headline: Music technology sits between a record-breaking music industry and the digital skills the whole Creative Industries sector needs more of.

subject: Drama & Theatre
headline: Theatre-makers and arts producers are named on the UK's shortage list as the Creative Industries expands towards 2030.

subject: Dance
headline: Dance is one of the clearest cases in the arts: skilled dancers sit on the UK's own shortage list for skilled worker visas.

subject: Physical Education
headline: PE opens routes into a coaching and sport workforce that is professionalising fast — paid coaching roles rose from 38% to 53% in two years.

subject: Sport & Exercise Science
headline: Sport science feeds a growing performance and coaching industry, and routes into the allied health workforce the NHS is expanding.

subject: Food Science & Nutrition
headline: Food science feeds the UK's largest manufacturing sector by jobs, which is investing to close a skills gap twice the size of the wider average.
